findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14(B) Cooling. (B) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours to 5°C (41°F) or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature, such as reconstituted FOODS and canned tuna. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the follow nonfood-contact surfaces in need of more frequent cleaning:
(i) the underside of the soda fountain where several residues have accumulated;
(ii) the hose going into the fan in the walk-in cooler where a significant amount of ice has accumulated.
Ensure that these areas are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of residues by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing (THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION). Additionally, several times during the inspection employees almost re-entered the kitchen or put on gloves without handwashing but the PIC intervened and instructed them to wash hands. The PIC should focus on hand washing education for all employees. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed there are several holes in the mop sink wall. These holes must be filled (ex.caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the holes are sealed by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived. The PIC stated that an employee had dumped the bucket after lunch but it was not remade. A sanitizer bucket was filled during the inspection testing at 400 ppm (quat). Ensure that there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the fans in the walk-in cooler (THIS IS A FIRST REPAET VIOLATION) and walk-in freezer have an accumulation of dust. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure that the fans are cleaned to the sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Observed there is not employee health reporting forms at the facility. There needs to be employee reporting forms signed by the employees stating they will report to the PIC about their health and activities related to diseases transmissible through food. The inspector provided employee reporting forms to the PIC. Ensure these forms are signed by all employees before the follow-up date of 07/08/2024.

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed that an employee turned off the faucet handles with their barehand after washing their hands. Failure to use a barrier to turn off the faucet handles recontaminates clean hands. The inspector talked to the PIC and they will educated their employees on the proper hand-washing procedure. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed that the inside top-potion of the ice machine surrounding the baffles has an accumulation of soil, including pink mold. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch. A follow-up on 07/08/2024 will occur to ensure that the accumulation of soil and mold in the ice machine has been cleaned.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the following needs cleaned inside of the walk-in cooler: (1) dust on the blades of the fan; (2) soil on the floors. Ensure that these surfaces inside the walk-in cooler are cleaned at a frequently necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of soil and mold underneath the ice machine. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. There is a leak occurring from the ice machine that could be contributing to the mold build-up. During the 07/08/2024 follow-up, inspectors will be checking up on the soil and mold beneath the ice machine. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that the PIC did not have food handler certificates for the employees. Ensure that all employees get their food handlers certification within 30 days of hiring, and that copies of all the certificates are held at the facility.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
The hand sink in the kitchen is actively dripping from the drain pipe. All plumbing fixtures must be maintained in good repair. Ensure that the hand sink is repaired by the next routine inspection. 

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION ON 07/28/2022.

Inspector observed a wet mop stored with the mop head on the floor of the utility sink. Mops must be stored in a manner that prevents contamination and facilitates air drying. Mops may be stored in the upper portion of the mop bucket and/or hanging inverted along the wall. Ensure that mops are stored properly at the next routine inspection. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
A personal phone was observed on the counter where food preparation occurs. Ensure that staff have a designated area available to put personal items and that personal items are not stored in locations which may contaminate foods/food-preparation areas. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
A spray bottle containing a blue cleaner was observed hanging on the edge of the hand sink without any label. All cleaners must be clearly labeled. Operator removed the spray bottle and labeled appropriately. Corrected on site. 

7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Personal drinks including a Dr. Pepper and a bottled iced coffee were in the walk in cooler above food. Operator moved these drinks to an appropriate location. Personal drinks must be stored in a location away from food and food preparation areas to prevent contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
A mop was stored head down in the mop sink. Ensure that mops are hung inverted and off the ground to prevent dripping down the wall and allow air drying or sitting in the top portion of the mop bucket. Operator hung the mop during the inspection. Corrected on site. 

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: No employee health documentation was provided. Employee health documentation must be present for all employees. Ensure all employees demonstrate knowledge of responsibility of reporting. Food Employee Reporting Agreement was provided to facility.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility does not have written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy or kit. CORRECTED— Inspector provided policy. Post or keep on file for reference in case of vomit/diarrhea events.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Sliced tomatoes in the prep cooler observed at 51F (probed). CORRECTED— PIC stated that tomatoes are cut daily and that the tomatoes observed had been removed from the lower portion of the cooler an hour ago. PIC moved tomatoes to lower (colder) portion of the cooler to cool them down to 41F or below. All other items in the cooler were observed to be 41F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Opened half-gallon of buttermilk and a plastic container of sauce observed without date marking. CORRECTED— PIC labeled foods with the dates they were opened or prepared. Ensure all foods are labeled with when they were opened or prepared.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Damp mop observed mop-end down in the mop sink. Store damp mops in a position that promotes air drying.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment: No employee health documentation was provided. Employee Health documentation must be present for all employees. Ensure all employees demonstrate knowledge of responsibility of reporting. Form 1-B Employee health form provided. Reference 2-102.11

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: Observed walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer to have inadequate lighting. Lights were either missing or not working. Ensure adequate lighting is present in food areas.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
(REPEAT #1) No CFM was present during inspection. Ensure adequate amount of CFMs are present for full coverage of food operation. Obtain CFM. Reference 750.540.
(TD* #2 was changed to #1) 8/20/2019

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed walk-in freezer to have ice build-up. In addition, ice appears to drip onto food containers. Ensure frost build-up is prevented. Also, protect food from potential cross-contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No FSSMC present in facility. All category II facilities must have a FSSMC present in facility for at least 35 hours per week. 

Employee provided district manager's CFM license. However, no adequate proof provided suggesting district manager works a full-work week at facility. 
Brian Potthoff
11844974 12/27/19
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: No FSSMC present. FSSMC must be present (on work schedule) in all category II Facilities.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Observed food boxes stored under leaking condenser line in walk-in freezer. Food cannot be stored under condenser without proper protection. Condenser must be in good repair to prevent leaking, food must be stored properly to prevent potential cross contamination.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitation bucket present upon inspection. Sanitation buckets must be made and capable of use during all times of food prep. Employee corrected violation with 200ppm Quat sanitation bucket.
750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed red bull can inside refridgerator used for food prep. All personal items must be in designated area away from food storage and food prep areas. 
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No FSSMC is present. All category II facilities must have a FSSMC employed full-time.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed boxes of food stored under a leaking condenser line in the walk in freezer. Boxes were removed from under the line to correct the violation. Facility management states that the unit has been serviced by Henson Robinson in June and Airmasters in October. Until the unit has been repaired, facility shall not store boxes of food under this condenser line. Food shall be protected at all times during storage.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of frost build up in the walk in freezer. Defrost freezer. Managment states that they have already contacted maintenace company. 
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer concentration in the three compartment sink to be 10 ppm Cl-. When discussed with staff, employee stated that they had just wash, rinse, sanitized the meat slicer. When asked if the employee had tested the concentration, they replied no they had not. Sanitizer was remade while inspectors were on-site to correct the violation. Final sanitizer concentration was 50 ppm Cl-.750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a wet wiping cloth to be stored on the three compartment sink. Wet wiping cloths should be stored in clean sanitizer solution when not in use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed a bottle of blue liquid to be unlabeled and stored on a box of chips. Store toxic substances way from food. 
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a bottle of blue liquid to be unlabeled. When discussed with management, bottle was identified as glass cleaner and a label was provided. Label all toxic substances.
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Absence of labeling on salt container in the back--bottles of dressing up front in the 2 dr cooler unit. Label all food items. (corrected)
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the back of the handsinks in both restrooms to be cracking caulk at the wall. Replace the caulk.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed mounds of ice on the walkin freezer floor. Clean the floor of ice.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Single service food containers were stored food side up on the wire shelves in the back room.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.
Cover or invert the containers.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Two spray bottles of cleaner were not labeled as to their contents.

750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

The bottles were labeled to correct the violation.
